# Technology Evaluation: AI Gateway

**Status:** In Progress
**Date:** 2026-05-31
**Author:** Mike Goppert
**Scorecard:** [EVAL-ai-gateway.xlsx](EVAL-ai-gateway.xlsx)
**Security Guidance:** [GUID-SEC-AI-GW-2.9.07](../../guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/GUID-SEC-AI-GW-2.9.07.md)

[strategy/tech-evals/ai-gateway/EVAL-ai-gateway.md#context]

## Context

Gainwell requires a centralized AI Gateway to serve as a dedicated security enforcement plane between consuming applications and AI model endpoints. Per GUID-SEC-AI-GW-2.9.07, the AI Gateway must provide capabilities architecturally distinct from the enterprise API gateway: prompt/response routing policy, guardrail and content safety enforcement, token-aware rate limiting, DLP inspection, external AI provider governance, and AI-specific audit evidence generation.

The AI Gateway is a mandatory component for all production AI service topologies and must support HIPAA compliance requirements including BAA-governed routing, PHI protection, and 6-year audit retention.

Additional requirements:

- **MCP server hosting** — the gateway must proxy and govern MCP (Model Context Protocol) server connections, applying the same enforcement pipeline (auth, DLP, audit) to tool invocations
- **Per-user resource tracking** — track model/resource usage at the individual Gainwell user level for chargeback and governance
- **Model downgrade policies** — ability to substitute a requested model with a lower-cost/lower-tier model based on policy (e.g., route GPT-4 requests to GPT-3.5 when appropriate)
- **Backup/fallback models** — automatic failover to backup models when primary models are unavailable or degraded

## Decision Tree Position

**Level 2** — Identify the best ROI 3rd party or open source platform/tool for the capability. No existing internal solution fulfills the full AI gateway requirement. Existing vendor relationships with Databricks and Kong are relevant factors.

### Business Criteria (15%)

| # | Criterion | Weight | Description |

| 1 | Customer & community support | 5 | Active community, documentation quality, forums, knowledge base, and responsiveness to issues and feature requests |

### Financial Criteria (20%)

| # | Criterion | Weight | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Budget controls & thresholds | 10 | Hard spending caps and alert thresholds per team/workspace/user; automatic enforcement when budgets are exceeded |

### Operations Criteria (10%)

| # | Criterion | Weight | Description |

| 1 | CI/CD & IaC support | 10 | Terraform provider, declarative config (GitOps), API-driven provisioning for pipeline automation |

### Security & Compliance Criteria (25%)

| AI Security Domain | Evaluation Criterion | Weight | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data Protection | PII & Sensitive Data Controls | 10 | Classify, redact, tokenize, or block regulated data (PII/PHI) in prompts, files, and responses before AI processing |
| Data Protection | Vector Database Security | 10 | Secure vector stores with encryption, access controls, tenant isolation, and query rate limiting |
| Data Protection | Embedding Confidentiality | 8 | Prevent re-identification and semantic leakage from embeddings derived from sensitive content |
| Data Protection | Data Retention & Deletion | 8 | Enforce lifecycle policies, legal holds, and cryptographic erasure for AI-related data |
| Data Protection | Data Integrity & Provenance | 5 | Validate dataset integrity and maintain verifiable lineage for training and retrieval data |
| Data Protection | Data Residency Controls | 8 | Enforce data sovereignty requirements by routing AI workloads to compliant geographic regions |
| Prompt Security | Prompt Injection Defense | 10 | Detect and neutralize prompt injection attacks across inputs, retrieval content, and tool responses |
| Prompt Security | Jailbreak & Policy Bypass Detection | 10 | Identify attempts to bypass safety policies, override roles, or escalate capabilities |
| Prompt Security | System Prompt Protection | 8 | Protect hidden instructions and routing policies from disclosure or unauthorized modification |
| Prompt Security | Content Safety Filtering | 8 | Filter unsafe, prohibited, or policy-violating content in both inputs and outputs |
| Access Control / IAM | Identity & Access Management | 10 | Enforce authentication, authorization, RBAC/ABAC, and least-privilege access to AI resources |
| Access Control / IAM | Secret & Credential Protection | 10 | Prevent secrets, tokens, and credentials from entering or leaking through AI systems |
| Access Control / IAM | Network Segmentation & Isolation | 8 | Segment AI workloads with private endpoints, VPCs, and zero-trust network controls |
| Agent / Tool Security | Tool Allow-listing & Authorization | 10 | Restrict agent tool access to approved, vetted tools with explicit authorization controls |
| Agent / Tool Security | Execution Sandboxing | 10 | Run tool executions in isolated, constrained environments with resource limits |
| Agent / Tool Security | Human-in-the-Loop for High-Risk Actions | 10 | Require human approval before agents execute destructive, sensitive, or irreversible actions |
| Agent / Tool Security | Outbound Access Controls | 8 | Restrict and monitor agent outbound network, API, and data egress |
| Model Security | Model Registry & Versioning | 8 | Maintain controlled registry with versioned, signed model artifacts and deployment eligibility |
| Model Security | Model Drift & Behavior Monitoring | 8 | Monitor model outputs for drift, degradation, and anomalous behavior patterns |
| Model Security | Model Supply Chain Security | 5 | Validate signed artifacts, SBOMs, and attestations for model dependencies |
| Monitoring & Observability | Prompt & Output Logging | 10 | Log all prompts, responses, tool calls, and moderation actions for audit and investigation |
| Monitoring & Observability | SIEM Integration & Alerting | 8 | Stream AI security events to SIEM with real-time alerting on anomalies and threats |
| Monitoring & Observability | Execution Audit Trail | 8 | Maintain immutable audit logs of agent actions, tool invocations, and decision paths |
| Monitoring & Observability | Per-User Resource Tracking | 8 | Track and attribute AI resource consumption, costs, and usage patterns per user or service |
| Governance / Compliance | AI Security Policy Framework | 10 | Document and enforce AI-specific security policies, standards, and acceptable use |
| Governance / Compliance | Risk Classification & Assessment | 8 | Classify AI use cases by risk tier and conduct appropriate impact assessments |
| Governance / Compliance | Vendor Security Due Diligence | 8 | Evaluate third-party AI vendors for security, privacy, and compliance requirements |
| Governance / Compliance | Incident Response for AI Systems | 8 | Define and test incident response procedures specific to AI-related security events |
| Governance / Compliance | BAA-Governed Routing | 10 | Route PHI and sensitive healthcare data only through BAA-covered AI services and endpoints |

### Technical Criteria (30%)

| # | Criterion | Weight | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A/B testing & canary release | 2 | Traffic splitting for model experiments; gradual rollout of new models with automatic rollback on error threshold |
| 2 | API gateway integration | 2 | Ability to sit behind or integrate with existing enterprise API gateways (Kong, Azure APIM, Apigee) |
| 3 | Automatic retries & exponential backoff | 5 | Retry failed requests with configurable backoff strategy; handle transient provider errors without application-level retry logic |
| 4 | Concurrency management | 5 | Control concurrent request limits per consumer/identity to prevent resource exhaustion |
| 5 | Context propagation & metadata enrichment | 5 | Pass identity, data sensitivity tier, and routing context through the enforcement pipeline via headers, metadata, or structured context |
| 6 | Cost-aware routing with model downgrade | 5 | Substitute a requested model with a lower-cost alternative based on policy (e.g., route simple queries to cheaper models) |
| 7 | Domain federation | 10 | Delegated governance — each business unit/team manages their own budgets, allowed models, and guardrails under a central enterprise policy |
| 8 | Fail-closed on unavailability | 10 | When the gateway itself is down, all AI traffic is blocked — never bypassed directly to model endpoints. Per GUID-SEC-AI-GW-2.9.07 |
| 9 | Failover / fallback routing | 10 | Automatic failover to backup models when primary is unavailable or degraded; circuit-breaker pattern with health checks |
| 10 | Latency-aware routing | 5 | Dynamically route to the lowest-latency provider/endpoint based on real-time performance metrics |
| 11 | Load testing evidence | 2 | Published benchmarks or customer-verifiable load testing demonstrating performance at enterprise scale |
| 12 | MCP DLP inspection | 5 | Apply DLP/PII inspection to MCP tool inputs and outputs before they cross security boundaries |
| 13 | MCP protocol support | 10 | Native Model Context Protocol support: HTTP+SSE transport, tool routing, server registry, protocol-aware enforcement |
| 14 | MCP server hosting | 10 | Host and proxy MCP servers through the gateway with the same enforcement pipeline (auth, audit, DLP) applied to tool invocations |
| 15 | MCP tool invocation audit | 5 | Audit logging of all MCP tool calls with identity, tool name, parameters, and outcome for compliance |
| 16 | MCP tool-call governance | 10 | Authorization and access control at the individual MCP tool level; policy-based tool allowlisting per consumer |
| 17 | Model version control & pinning | 5 | Pin specific model versions in production; track model lineage; prevent unexpected model changes |
| 18 | Multi-agent support | 2 | Govern multi-agent orchestration where multiple AI agents collaborate; track context across agent-to-agent calls |
| 19 | Multi-modal support | 5 | Route and govern text, vision, audio, and embedding requests — not just chat completions |
| 20 | Multi-model support | 10 | Route to all major LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, AWS Bedrock, open-source) through a single gateway |
| 21 | On-prem / hybrid LLM support | 10 | Ability to route to self-hosted models (vLLM, Ollama, custom endpoints) alongside cloud providers |
| 22 | OpenTelemetry export | 5 | Export metrics, traces, and logs via OTLP standard to plug into existing enterprise observability (Datadog, Grafana, Splunk) |
| 23 | Plugin/extension framework | 5 | Extensibility via custom plugins, middleware hooks, or webhook integrations for organization-specific logic |
| 24 | Policy-based routing | 10 | Route requests based on data sensitivity tier, cost targets, latency requirements, or risk classification — not just static load balancing |
| 25 | RAG integration | 2 | Native support for retrieval-augmented generation workflows (vector search, context injection) |
| 26 | REST/gRPC APIs | 5 | Management and proxy APIs available via REST and/or gRPC for programmatic integration |
| 27 | SDKs & developer tooling | 2 | Language SDKs, CLI tools, and developer experience for integrating applications with the gateway |
| 28 | SLA & availability monitoring | 5 | Built-in health checks and availability metrics for all upstream model endpoints; alerting on degradation |
| 29 | Streaming response proxy | 10 | Proxy SSE/WebSocket streaming responses with enforcement (guardrails, DLP) applied during or after stream — not bypassed |
| 30 | Throughput & enforcement latency | 10 | Handle enterprise-scale TPS; enforcement pipeline overhead must stay under 200ms for interactive applications per GUID-SEC-AI-GW-2.9.07 |
| 31 | Timeout configuration | 5 | Fine-grained timeout controls (connect, read, write) per route/provider to prevent hung requests |
| 32 | Token-aware rate limiting | 10 | Rate limits based on token consumption (not just request count); per-user/per-app token budgets with configurable thresholds |
| 33 | Unified abstraction API | 10 | Single API interface that abstracts provider differences; applications don't change code when switching models |

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selected vendor lacks native BAA routing enforcement | HIPAA non-compliance; PHI routed to uncovered endpoints | Require custom policy layer or compensating controls at network tier |
| Vendor lock-in to a platform-specific gateway | Limits multi-cloud flexibility | Prefer vendors with self-hosted option and standard APIs |
| Netskope product maturity for AI Gateway use case | SASE-first product may lack deep AI routing/orchestration features | Evaluate feature depth against purpose-built AI gateway competitors |
| Gateway becomes single point of failure | All AI capabilities unavailable if gateway fails | Require HA deployment with fail-closed behavior per GUID-SEC-AI-GW-2.9.07 |
